title: Orthogonal session-level cost fingerprinter with confidence bounds
creator: Maya Reynolds
description:
Problem: Current billing attribution aggregates at coarse windows and struggles with interleaved multi-route requests, late-arriving tokens, and prefix/KV cache effects. This makes per-session line-item cost broken out by model/route/quantization hard to explain in the console and prevents accurate near-real-time anomaly detection.

Goal: Build a streaming 'cost fingerprinter' service that annotates per-request and per-session records with deterministic, explainable cost line-items plus a confidence interval that reflects uncertainty from late-arrivals, sampling, and cache hits. Outputs must power Console dashboards (per-route cost breakdown), alerts (spend regressions), and downstream invoicing jobs.

Scope:
- A lightweight protobuf envelope appended to existing request events with fields: model_variant, routed_path, token_count_estimate, cache_hit_adjustment, quantization_profile, kernel_class_hint, cost_estimate_usd, confidence_upper, confidence_lower, provenance_tags.
- Streaming assembler that consumes gateway events, KV-cache delta events, and kernel-exec telemetry; produces enriched records to the billing topic (kafka: billing.fingerprints) with idempotency keys for replay.
- A downstream consumer for Console that materializes per-session line items into Clickhouse daily partitions and emits anomaly signals to our alerting service.
- Backfill/compare job to reconcile historical invoices for the canary tenant subset.

Non-goals: not handling final invoicing adjustments, not replacing ledger reconciliation jobs here. This component focuses on near-real-time attribution for observability and early-warning.

Success metrics:
- Fingerprint event processing 99th percentile latency < 250ms from request completion to fingerprint emission for 95% of tenants.
- Console per-route cost breakdown accuracy within 2% compared to settled ledger for canary tenants (after backfill reconciliation).
- Drop in false-positive spend alerts by >= 30% in first month after rollout for canary tenants.
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with Console, Billing, and Runtime teams. Agreed on proto schema draft and required telemetry joins (gateway request id, session id, kernel trace id). Assigned Diego as owner for streaming assembler and Priya for Clickhouse materializer.

2026-02-20: Prototype producer implemented (nodejs) that pulls gateway events and emits minimal fingerprint records. Initial perf locally ~18ms per event. Opened PR: github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-fingerprint/pull/7. Waiting design review on provenance tagging scheme.

2026-02-28: Design review completed. Trade-offs discussed: attaching full kernel traces vs. kernel hints to keep fingerprint record size small. Decided to include kernel_class_hint and sample kernel_trace_id only for 0.1% of requests to support debugging. Recorded decision in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/METER/Cost+Fingerprinter+Design.

2026-03-04: Load test against staging kafka cluster with synthetic interleaved sessions (~5k rps). Observed 99th latency at 410ms due to serde overhead. Implemented compact proto layout and batching — latency reduced to 190ms. Added serializer optimization ticket ENG-441333 as dependency.

2026-03-09: Canary plan created. Will onboard 5 early-adopter tenants with limited retention (7 days) and enable backfill comparison against ledger for 3 days. Console UI team prepared a per-session view to display line items (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/3452).

2026-03-12: Deployed streaming assembler to canary region with feature flag. Observed a production anomaly: quantization_profile missing on ~0.6% of events due to older runtime agents. Added imputation fallback and created dependency ticket ENG-441450 to patch runtime telemetry.
